The procedures were performed with no complications.

report.source_text: In the intensive care unit, the patient remained ventilated and sedated for 3 days. Initial sedation consisted of 1% propofol at 15 ml/h and alfentanil at 4 ml/h, requiring metaraminol support at 2.5 ml/h. Heavy sedation was stopped on day 2 with the aim of extubation, though the patient struggled with severe pain resulting from the rib fractures, and further light sedation with remifentanil at 6.3 ml/h was required. With successful extubation, the patient’s chest drains were removed, and there were no reported complications.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A white British female in her 70s presented to the emergency department after falling onto a metal oven (aga) with right-sided chest pain and shortness of breath. Physical examination revealed rapidly progressive extensive subcutaneous emphysema with crepitus affecting the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and upper limbs, causing palpebral closure, vocal changes, and stridor. Despite oxygen saturation of 90% on high-flow oxygen, other vital signs remained normal without hemodynamic compromise. The patient required emergent intubation due to airway compromise. Chest X-ray demonstrated severe subcutaneous emphysema obscuring visualization of pneumothoraces. CT imaging confirmed right-sided rib fractures (ribs 7, 8, and 9 in two places) without flail chest, a right-sided moderate-volume pneumothorax with lower-lobe pulmonary hemorrhage, and a left-sided moderate-volume pneumothorax with lower-lobe laceration and collapse. Bilateral 28Fr chest drains were inserted in the emergency department, initially draining air, without complications. The patient remained hemodynamically stable throughout, confirming absence of tension physiology. She was transferred to the intensive care unit, remained ventilated for 3 days, and was successfully extubated on day 3 with chest drains subsequently removed without complications. At 1-month follow-up, recovery was good with return to usual activities despite residual fatigue and weakness that progressively improved over several months.
